title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
summary: Ketonaemia ≥3.0 mmol/L + glucose >11 mmol/L (or known diabetes) + pH <7.3 or bicarbonate <15 — fixed-rate insulin and fluids on a structured pathway.

sources.label: JBDS-IP — Management of DKA in adults (via ABCD)
NICE NG17 — Type 1 diabetes in adults (DKA section)

blocks.title: Severe DKA — involve critical care if
blocks.body: pH <7.1, bicarbonate <5 mmol/L, ketones >6 mmol/L, K⁺ <3.5 on admission, GCS <12, SpO₂ <92% on air, SBP <90, pulse >100 or <60, or anion gap >16 with deteriorating trend.

items: ABCDE; VBG (pH, K⁺, glucose), capillary ketones, U&E, FBC, cultures if infection suspected, ECG
Look for the precipitant: infection, missed insulin, first presentation, MI, pregnancy, SGLT2 inhibitor (may be euglycaemic)
Weigh or estimate weight for insulin rate
Continue the patient's usual long-acting basal insulin

blocks.title: First hours of management (adapt to local DKA pathway)

steps.detail: 0.9% sodium chloride 1 L IV over 1 h (faster 500 mL bolus over 10–15 min if SBP <90, then reassess). Typical continuation: 1 L over 2 h ×2, then 1 L over 4 h ×2 — verify against local policy and adjust for age/heart failure.
steps.branch: SBP <90 despite 2 boluses → senior + critical care review

steps.detail: Soluble insulin 0.1 units/kg/hour IV (e.g. 50 units in 50 mL 0.9% saline). Do not bolus. Aim: ketones falling ≥0.5 mmol/L/h, bicarbonate rising ≥3 mmol/L/h, glucose falling ≥3 mmol/L/h — verify against local policy.
steps.branch: Targets not met → check infusion/access, then increase rate per pathway

steps.detail: Add KCl to the second and subsequent fluid bags per the potassium table below. Check K⁺ on VBG at 1 h, 2 h, then 2-hourly — verify against local policy.
steps.branch: K⁺ <3.5 → senior review; insulin may need to be held per local pathway

steps.detail: Add 10% glucose 125 mL/h alongside saline; continue fixed-rate insulin until ketones <0.6, pH >7.3 (do not stop insulin just because glucose normalises).

When resolved AND eating/drinking: give fast-acting subcutaneous insulin with a meal and stop the infusion 30–60 min after. Involve the diabetes team, address the precipitant, review before discharge.

headers: KCl in each litre of fluid
rows: Senior review — needs higher-rate replacement, usually with cardiac monitoring

blocks.title: Watch for
blocks.body: Hypokalaemia and hypoglycaemia are the commonest iatrogenic harms. Cerebral oedema (especially in young adults) — new headache, irritability, falling GCS — is an emergency. Beware euglycaemic DKA with SGLT2 inhibitors: ketones and pH matter more than the glucose.

blocks.title: Why fixed-rate insulin?
blocks.body: The goal in DKA is to switch off ketogenesis, not merely to lower glucose. A weight-based fixed rate reliably suppresses lipolysis and hepatic ketone production; glucose is then kept up with 10% dextrose so insulin can continue until the ketoacidosis — the actual disease — has resolved.
